Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Consuming UV-exposed mushrooms did not improve depression outcomes compared with control; no between-group differences in brain health indices.
Sentence: "Consuming UV light-exposed mushrooms did not improve brain health outcomes."
Measured as: depression (BDI-II, PHQ-9)
Population: Adults without severe depression, cardiovascular disease, or Type 2 Diabetes, age 43 ± 11 y, BMI 29.8 kg/m2
Intervention: Two daily servings (168 g/d) of UV-exposed cremini mushrooms providing ~800 IU/d vitamin D2 for 6 weeks
Comparator: 2 tsp/d breadcrumbs (control)
Design: non-randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 41
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation reduced depression scores more than placebo at 38-40 weeks of gestation.
Sentence: "While, the vitamin D group had greater reduction in depression scores than the control group at 38-40 weeks of gestation (p = 0.01) also, at 4 and 8 weeks after birth (p < 0.001)."
Measured as: depression score (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression scale) at 38-40 weeks of gestation
Population: Pregnant women in Shiraz, Iran, 18 or older, gestational age 26-28 weeks, baseline depression score 0-13, no history of mental illness
Intervention: Vitamin D3 2000 IU daily from 26-28 weeks of gestation until childbirth
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 169
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
